GainsBlock.rationale: `public override bool GainsBlock => true` (Fisticuffs.cs:17) == the class attribute. Load-bearing because Fisticuffs has no printed block number, exactly the case cards/base.py:65-69 cites.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Fisticuffs.cs:21-24) == cost 1 / ATTACK / UNCOMMON / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(7m, ValueProp.Move)` (Fisticuffs.cs:19) == `_damage = 7`, powered on both sides.

OnPlay.issue: The attack is faithful and the block prop set is right (`ValueProp.Move`, powered, so not in G1's blast radius). THE BLOCK AMOUNT IS COMPUTED FROM A DIFFERENT QUANTITY. C# gains `attackCommand.Results.SelectMany(r => r).Sum(r => r.TotalDamage + r.OverkillDamage)` (Fisticuffs.cs:32), and those two fields are precisely defined: `TotalDamage => BlockedDamage + UnblockedDamage` (DamageResult.cs:64) with `UnblockedDamage = currentHp - CurrentHp` and `OverkillDamage = num - currentHp` when the blow kills (Creature.LoseHpInternal, Creature.cs:445-457). So C#'s figure is blocked + hp-actually-lost + overkill, i.e. the ENTIRE post-modifier damage the attack put out. The sim uses the return value of `DamageCmd.deal`, which is `hp_lost` (cmds.py:126) -- the middle term only. It therefore grants LESS block than the game whenever the target had block or was overkilled. Observable and ordinary: hit a 5-HP enemy for 7 and the game grants 7 block while the sim grants 5; hit an enemy holding 10 block for 7 and the game grants 7 while the sim grants 0. LIVE -- Fisticuffs is a ported Uncommon colorless Attack, enemy block is routine, and overkill is the normal case late in a fight. RATIONALE CITES THIRD FILES (rule 7): DamageResult.cs, Creature.cs and cmds.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: the sim skips the block gain entirely when nothing got through (`if dealt > 0`, colorless_attacks.py:109)
guards.rationale: C# calls GainBlock with the summed value unconditionally, and a sum of 0 gains nothing. The two agree on a fully-blocked hit ONLY because the sim's figure is 0 there anyway -- C#'s would be the full TotalDamage, which is the OnPlay entry's finding, not this guard's.
